sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text: We could not read any of Pessac's own rules on street parking, because the municipality's website refused automated access, so this briefing rests on Bordeaux Métropole and its operators. The Métropole's low-emission zone has applied inside the ring road, 24 hours a day, since 1 January 2025; unclassified vehicles can no longer drive or park there, and eleven park-and-rides remain reachable by dedicated access roads, two of them in Pessac, Bougnard and Unitec [13]. In November 2021 the Métropole and 16 higher-education institutions launched a joint mobility plan for the 235-hectare Pessac-Talence-Gradignan campus, which hosts about 60,000 students and 10,000 staff, with the stated aim of reducing congestion in parking and traffic [15]. A university page says a study of the roughly 11,000 spaces on the campus found the car parks overall very oversized, with more than 4,000 spaces still free at the busiest point of the day; the study is undated, so treat the figure as indicative [14].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text: The development has been in the town-centre car park and the park-and-ride offer. METPARK renovated the 343-space Pessac Centre underground car park over more than five months in 2025 while it stayed open, with a repaint costing close to 870,000 euros, redesigned circulation and ticketless plate-recognition entry; the commune renovated the access tunnel [6]. The car park has 50 EV charge points, 48 slow and 2 fast, inaugurated on 26 June 2025, and a METSTATION cycle hub planned on level -1 [7]. A secure TBM bike shelter with 19 places opened at Pessac Centre station in May 2025 [17]. Since July 2021 the city and METPARK have offered two hours of free parking in the town-centre car park [4], and since 3 October 2022 TBM card holders can park free there if they use public transport that day [5]. The Métropole voted a tariff on 29 September 2023 allowing two-to-five-day stays in selected park-and-rides, including Cap Métiers and Pessac Alouette [12]. A 2015 press kit expected the tram B branch to France Alouette to carry 10,000 new passengers a day and planned a 160-space park-and-ride near Cap Métiers; TBM now lists 148 and 144 spaces [16].

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
METPARK, the Métropole's parking authority, runs Pessac Centre, open 24/7 about 100 m from the TER station, with free parking under two hours, then 4.80 euros for two hours and 9 euros for four to 24 hours; monthly subscriptions cost 70 euros, or 50 for residents [2][3]. TBM runs the park-and-rides: Unitec (249 spaces), Bougnard (168), Gare de Pessac Alouette (148) and Cap Métiers (144, season-ticket holders only), with Arts & Métiers (593, in Talence) at the campus [0]. Pessac Centre as a TBM park-and-ride is for season-ticket holders on weekdays [1]. Same-day park-and-ride parking is included in a TBM subscription, and others pay 4.50 euros for seven round trips [9]; residents within 500 m of Gare de Pessac Alouette can park overnight for 300 euros a year [10].

Our data cover five car parks with about 1,100 spaces, of which four have usable histories since 24 September 2026: Pessac Centre (400 spaces in the feed), Unitec (218), Bougnard (180) and Cap Métiers (146). Occupancy averaged about 20% on weekdays and 12% at weekends, weighted by spaces. Pessac Centre is the busiest at 29% on weekdays, while the park-and-rides are lightly used: Unitec 19%, Bougnard 16% and Cap Métiers 4%. Gare de Pessac Alouette has only two days of readings. These are about four weeks of data.
